players.name: António João Pereira de Albuquerque Tavares da Silva

1.headline: Haaland doubles, captains disappoint — and Rob wins the highest-scoring poker game of the week by one
1.introduction: Gameweek 1 arrived like a packed pub on a Friday: loud, slightly chaotic and full of people who think they know better. Few surprises — plenty of Haaland captains, a ridiculous amount of 11s from João Pedro and Ødegaard, and enough bench crimes to keep the WhatsApp roast lively for a week.

matches.title: Richard 56 v Prince Majid Rd FC 57 — Rich gets mugged by one point
matches.text: Rich (Richard) lost by the thinnest of margins to Rami (Prince Majid Rd FC), 56–57. Both managers doubled up on familiar names but it was Rami’s Kiernan Dewsbury‑Hall (11) and Ødegaard (11) that squeaked him over the line. Rich’s captain pick (Bruno) delivered a grand total of 4 after being doubled — neat and conservative, like someone who pays to sit in the corner of a pub and criticises the DJ.

matches.title: Humorous Name United 72 v Roped in again 71 — highest-scoring game, narrowest heart attacks
matches.text: Rob (Humorous Name United) edged Paul (Roped in again) 72–71 in the week’s top thriller — the 143 combined points made it the highest-scoring match. Both sides had the usual suspects (João Pedro 11s, Ødegaard 11s) and both captains underwhelmed with doubles only producing 4s, but Rob’s balance of 11s and nines proved just enough. Paul can be proud: losing by one point in a shootout is the modern equivalent of being mugged while holding a winning lottery ticket.

matches.title: Change Name FC 67 v Bielsa's Babes 76 — Patrick turns up and turns over the league
matches.text: Patrick (Bielsa's Babes) posted the week’s highest single score, 76, to beat David (Change Name FC) 76–67. Patrick’s midfield returned plenty (Ødegaard 11, João Pedro 11) and his Haaland captain doubled — not spectacular, but everything else covered for him. David also captained Haaland but still finished on a respectable 67; both managers got the memo that piling up the 11s is a solid opening strategy.

matches.title: el Guapo 47 v BeLucky Again 51 — Tom has the week’s low and some brutal bench decisions
matches.text: Tom (el Guapo) managed the lowest score of GW1 with 47 and lost to Kev (BeLucky Again) 51–47. Tom’s starting XI included a tidy Marc Guéhi 10 and João Pedro 11, but he also left Granit Xhaka’s 9 on the bench with effective points 0 — a bench crime of the highest order. Kev won by being slightly less rubbish; he also committed his own bench sin, leaving Anton Stach’s 13 unused, but showed that 51 can still beat 47 when all else fails.

matches.title: FC Dangerous 50 v Seattle Scorchers 50 — the great stalemate
matches.text: Rob (FC Dangerous) and Andrew (Seattle Scorchers) obediently drew 50–50, proving once and for all that matching Captain Haaland doubles produce enthralling draws. Both sides had João Pedro 11 and similar supporting casts; nothing to see here except two managers who both either blocked each other out or refused to be the first to make a mistake.

matches.title: ChampagneSuperRovers 55 v Atletico Waspo 59 — Foz gets the points
matches.text: Ben (Atletico Waspo) beat James (ChampagneSuperRovers) 59–55. Ben’s João Pedro (11) and Joško Gvardiol (9) helped build a narrow win. James put in a decent showing — his Xhaka and João Pedro did the business — but it wasn’t quite enough to stop Ben taking the three points.

matches.title: Woolbrohampton 71 v Turf Less 50 — Ben W makes Martyn look properly poor
matches.text: Woolly (Woolbrohampton) humiliated Martyn (Turf Less) 71–50 — the biggest margin of GW1 at 21. Martyn’s Cole Palmer delivered a credible 13, but Ben simply piled on enough 11s and 9s (João Pedro 11, Szoboszlai 8, Calafiori 9) to make this a Sunday roast rather than a close contest. Martyn encountered the Burnley special: hope, then disappointment.

awards.text: 72–71 in the week’s highest-scoring match. Rob won the sort of game that gives everyone else withdrawal symptoms and a sudden urge to check their transfers twice next week.
Left Anton Stach's 13 pointless on the bench. That is criminal negligence in three counties.

awards.award: The Lowest Score (and Biggest Regret) Award
awards.text: Tom’s el Guapo managed a miserly 47 and benched Xhaka’s 9. He will tell you it was deliberate. We will not believe him.
A 21‑point win over Martyn and the biggest margin of GW1. If wealth could buy FPL form Ben’s bank account would have shown on Sunday.

1.table_commentary: The official Super 8s table — using H2H points and FPL points as the tie‑breaker — has Patrick (Bielsa's Babes) top after that 76, with Rob (Humorous Name United) second on 72 and Woolly (Woolbrohampton) third on 71. A cluster of managers follow on three points — Foz, Rami and Kev all picked up opening wins — while Watson and Andrew share a polite mid‑table draw. At the bottom, Martyn (Turf Less) and Tom (el Guapo) will be arguing over whose season is already ruined; both can thank their bench choices for giving them something to complain about.

preview.fixture: Prince Majid Rd FC v Woolbrohampton
preview.text: Rami hosts Woolly next. Both scored heavily in GW1 (57 and 71) and both roster João Pedro and a clutch of double‑figure midfielders, so this looks like an early shootout. If Rami’s Dewsbury‑Hall and Ødegaard turn up again, and Ben keeps converting those 9s and 11s, we’re in for a classic.

preview.fixture: Bielsa's Babes v Humorous Name United
preview.text: Patrick v Rob is GW2’s mini‑clash — top-of‑the‑table by the tie‑breaker and the next test for two managers who started well. Expect lots of the same names to be involved; captain choices will decide this one, as they did last week.

Martyn v James looks tasty only because Martyn’s Cole Palmer scored 13 despite the loss, while James had useful returns from Xhaka and João Pedro. If Martyn can stop self‑inflicting bench wounds he might make this competitive; otherwise James can stroll to three points.

1.closing: That’s your lot for GW1: a week of familiar faces delivering familiar returns, a catalogue of bench crimes and captains that underwhelmed. Keep the team screenshots coming — and someone please remind Kev that 13 on the bench is not a flex, it’s a misdemeanor. See you next Monday for more misery and occasional brilliance.
